start_here: Say to your AI: "List my files". It calls tool:your-files at @tools with tools:run and {call: {name: "list_files", arguments: {folder: "/"}}}; the engine starts the person's files session on the first call and every later call reaches the same one.
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it serves your files from your own store and keeps their names as rows in your own database.
instructions: 1. Make sure your files-store connection (your S3-compatible store: secret, key id, bucket, endpoint, region) and your database connection (own-rows-postgres-connection) are saved in your vault. tool:your-files is handed the files-store fields alone, and tool:your-files-names the database connection alone, each on the descriptor its row names and never printed: the engine lets one run reach only hosts every key it holds may go to.

2. Ask your AI for your files. Each ask is one call: tools:run at @tools with {tool: "tool:your-files", call: {name, arguments}}, where name is an operation of mcp-tools.json (list_files, list_changes, read_file_span, write_file, move_names, set_aside, make_folder, bounds, this_computer and the rest).
3. A device's folder (tools/files-on-every-device) makes the same calls through the same door, so a file saved there is the file your AI reads.

4. To share a file, say to your AI: "Share /Notes/a.txt for a day". share_file answers an address that opens the file by range (any size, in pieces or not) from the share byte route; stop it with stop_share (list_shares shows each share, never its key) and the next reader is refused. To share many files at one address, name them as items; give a video no browser plays a play form (a playable copy of it) and a poster form, and the share's page plays the copy and offers the original as a download.

worked_examples.title: List my files
worked_examples.given: A saved files-store connection and database connection.
worked_examples.hands_back: {tool: "tool:your-files", result: {structuredContent: {...}}}: the folder's names, each with its item, version and generation.

worked_examples.title: Follow what changed
worked_examples.ask: Tell me what changed in my files
worked_examples.given: A cursor (next) an earlier list_changes answered; without after it answers only the cursor of now.
worked_examples.hands_back: The changes after the cursor in the store's own order, each {op, kind, item, generation}, and next; with wait it waits for a change until the call's own time ends.
